name: Hatcheries

problems.words: Hatch results are on a register, I can't compare machines or egg sources
quick_ideas: Note egg source and machine against every hatch result
Look at a month of results side by side.

workzap_build.text: hatch results entered per batch, compared automatically by machine and egg source from the hatchery's own data.

problems.ask_first: How many setters and hatchers do you run?
problems.free_stops: The entry fields and comparison views go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one month's hatch results by machine and egg source on facing register pages, so weaker lines stand out for review.
Give one clerk the weekly job of copying each hatch result into one notebook section, so comparisons stop getting lost across registers.

problems.words: Bookings are on WhatsApp and we overbook some days
quick_ideas: Write each hatch day's capacity down and stop at it
Take bookings on one number only.

workzap_build.text: a booking calendar with a daily capacity limit, and written confirmations that would go to customers straight away.

problems.free_stops: Capacity rules and the confirmation flow are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count bookings against each hatch day's expected boxes in one notebook page, so crowded days are spotted before more promises go out.
Give one staff member the booking total for each hatch day and one booking notebook, so overbooking stops across scattered chats.

problems.words: Farmers cancel bookings when the rate drops and chicks are left over
quick_ideas: Put cancellation terms in writing at booking
Keep a waiting list to offer cancelled chicks to.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — cancellations tracked by customer, with waiting-list customers messaged automatically when chicks free up.

problems.ask_first: Do you take an advance with bookings?
problems.free_stops: The terms and waiting-list flow stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note cancelled bookings by hatch day and buyer type for one week, so you can see where leftover chicks usually come from.
Give one person the cancelled chicks list and one call round before dispatch, so spare boxes are offered while demand is still live.

problems.words: Customers say we sent fewer chicks than paid for
quick_ideas: Have the driver confirm box count at dispatch
Ask customers to confirm the count on receipt.

workzap_build.text: a dispatch sheet with box count, driver, times and delivery photo, recorded for every order.

problems.ask_first: Do you deliver, or do customers collect?
problems.free_stops: The dispatch record and confirmation steps go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare box counts at loading and on the delivery note for each trip, so short-count disputes can be checked quickly.
Give one dispatcher the job of writing every trip's box total in one register, so each complaint has one count to refer back to.

problems.words: Complaints of weak chicks come days later and we can't trace the batch
quick_ideas: Note egg source, machine and hatch date on every dispatch
Keep complaints against the batch, and take any pattern to your vet.

workzap_build.text: each hatch batch traced from egg source and machine to the customers who received it, so a complaint links back automatically.

problems.ask_first: How do complaints reach you now?
problems.free_stops: How batches are linked and traced is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at recent complaints beside dispatch dates and hatch sources in the register, so repeat trouble can be linked to one batch.
Give one dispatch clerk one notebook page per hatch batch for all outgoing boxes, so late complaints can be traced without guessing.

problems.words: Breeder farm sends eggs late or with too many cracked
quick_ideas: Count cracked and rejected eggs on arrival per source
Take a month's figures to the supplier.

workzap_build.text: egg intake logged by source with counts and photos, summarised per supplier automatically.

problems.ask_first: How many egg sources do you use?
problems.free_stops: The intake log and supplier summary go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count cracked eggs against each breeder farm arrival this week, so you can show which source is causing avoidable rejection.
Give one receiving staff member one arrival page per supplier load, so late deliveries and cracked eggs get logged the same way.

problems.words: Power failed during hatch and nobody alerted me
quick_ideas: Make one person on call every night, with numbers posted
Ask your equipment supplier what alarm outputs your machines already have.

workzap_build.text: custom_build — alerts from existing machine or generator alarms routed to on-call staff, with every outage logged.

problems.ask_first: Do your machines have any alarm output today?
problems.free_stops: How alarms are connected and routed stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every power interruption by time and who informed you this week, so the weak point in night alerting becomes visible.
Give one night person the owner call duty and one posted handover note, so outages reach you without waiting for someone else.

problems.words: Dealers take chicks on credit and pay late
quick_ideas: Confirm each credit order and due date in writing
Set your own credit limit per dealer.

workzap_build.text: a dealer ledger that keeps balances current and sends reminders automatically.

problems.ask_first: How many dealers buy on credit?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and limits are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare dealers with overdue balances against their latest chick pickups, so you can see which accounts keep extending without clearing.
Give one staff member one credit notebook and a fixed weekly review time, so overdue follow-up happens before the next dispatch.

problems.words: Lots of phone calls asking ‘is my order ready'
quick_ideas: Tell customers at booking when and how they'll hear
Send one message when chicks are ready.

workzap_build.text: automatic WhatsApp updates when chicks are ready and dispatched.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many orders go out on a busy day?
problems.free_stops: The update triggers and messages go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many ready-order calls come before dispatch time on one busy day, so you can see when customers start chasing updates.
Give one staff member the ready-order update duty at one fixed time daily, so callers hear back before the phone line gets jammed.

problems.words: Night staff skip checks or logging
quick_ideas: List the night checks as you already run them
Ask for a time-stamped entry for each.

workzap_build.text: a night checklist on the phone with timestamps, alerting the manager when a check is missed.

problems.ask_first: How do you know the night checks were done today?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and alert rules stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many night checks were logged versus due across one week, so you can see which shift is skipping the routine.
Give one night supervisor the logbook and one handover time each shift, so missed checks stop being argued about later.

never_say: Any incubation setting, chick vaccination, medicine, breeder nutrition or disease advice; suggest their vet or equipment supplier.
Anything that helps relabel chick grades or breeds, hide disease, or bypass import permits for eggs or parent stock.
Collecting customers' or drivers' IDs or bank details.

sample_reply.person: We run a broiler hatchery near Lahore. Bookings come by phone and WhatsApp into the manager's diary and we keep overbooking. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be brought under control, starting this week. 1. Fix each hatch day's capacity and stop taking bookings once it's reached. 2. Take all bookings on one number, so there's a single list. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a booking system with a daily capacity limit, written confirmations and ready/dispatched updates sent to every customer. Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you, or would you rather not?
